entry.title: 0.7.0 — radar: legend below chart, wider canvas, unknown ring (#72)
entry.content:
0.7.0 — radar: legend below chart, wider canvas, unknown ring (#72)

* 0.7.0 — topic radar: legend below the chart, wider canvas, larger web

The legend was already appended after the SVG, but `.cci-dash-topics-chart`
was `display: flex` with the default row direction, so the two sat side by
side and the legend ate the chart's width. Column direction puts it under the
graph, as intended.

While fixing that, found a latent clipping bug: the canvas was 200 units wide
with labels anchored at 1.28x a radius of 62, so the longest label
("Character") ran to x~216 and SVG clipped it at the viewBox edge. The canvas
is now 270x200 — deliberately wider than tall, since the web is circular but
the side labels extend horizontally — and the radius grows 62 -> 70, a 13%
larger web in the same vertical space.

RADAR_LAYOUT is exported so a test can assert the longest short label fits on
both sides. That regression shipped once already.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019M5G8xgvZWbLzRPRQk58n5

* 0.7.0 — topic radar: show unknown as a third ring in red

Unknown words were only implied by the gap between the outer ring and the
edge, which is not readable. The chart now draws three cumulative rings in the
same colour language the HSK coverage bars already use:

  green filled  fully known
  amber         + partially known
  red           + words explicitly marked unknown

The gap to the edge is now specifically "seen but not yet classified, or never
met", which is what it should have meant all along. `new` deliberately stays
out of the rings: the learner has encountered those words but made no
judgement, so counting them as classified would overstate coverage.

Tooltips gained the per-ring percentages, and tests pin the nesting invariant
(known <= known+partial <= classified) so an inner ring can never render
outside an outer one.

entry.content:
0.7.0 — topic radar: fix duplicate render, use short English labels, show partial (#71)

Three issues found in beta.1 testing.

1. The radar rendered twice. `renderTopicCoverageSection(root)` was called on
   two consecutive lines in renderDashboard — introduced by a scripted edit and
   a manual edit both applying, and missed because the verification grep was
   truncated by `| head`.

2. Axis labels were Chinese. They were chosen for compactness on a phone-width
   chart, but that makes the chart unreadable for a learner who cannot yet read
   the topic names — which is precisely the audience. Adds a `short` English
   label per topic (Food, Health, Travel …), short enough to fit the axes, with
   a test pinning length and uniqueness. Chinese remains available in the data.

3. Only fully-known words were visible. Partial words were folded into a single
   half-credited number the reader could not decompose. The chart now draws two
   nested rings in Coverage mode: filled = fully known, dashed = plus partially
   known, with the gap to the edge being unknown or never met. Tooltips give the
   full five-bucket split, and the footnote explains the reading.

`coverage` (known + half credit for partial) is retained as the input to
Relative mode, where a single derived number is the right shape.

Also fixes a lint Error the release guard caught: a static
`style.opacity` assignment in the legend, now a CSS class.

entry.title: 0.7.0 — topic coverage radar + safe prerelease workflow (#70)
entry.content:
0.7.0 — topic coverage radar + safe prerelease workflow (#70)

* 0.7.0 — safe prerelease workflow: stamp betas in CI, never in the default branch

Obsidian reads manifest.json on the default branch to decide which version to
advertise, then downloads assets from the release tagged identically to it. The
previous loop kept main's manifest pinned at the NEXT version while only
-rc.N prereleases existed, so every update check resolved to a release that did
not exist. check-release actively enforced that by stripping the suffix before
comparing.

BRAT, by contrast, reads manifest.json from the release ASSETS and is
"independent of the version numbering in the repository root", picking the
highest semver including prereleases. So the committed manifest must stay old
while the published assets must be new.

scripts/stamp-prerelease.mjs bridges the two: for a suffixed tag, CI stamps the
prerelease version into the working tree only. Nothing is committed, and the
whole gate then runs against the exact artifact that gets uploaded.

- check-release: tag must equal manifest.version EXACTLY; with no tag, a
  committed prerelease suffix is now a hard failure
- release.yml: conditional stamp step, plus artifact validation asserting the
  three files are non-empty and the asset manifest version equals the tag
- docs/release-process.md: full five-stage procedure, verified against Obsidian
  and BRAT documentation, with the stable promotion publishing the release
  BEFORE main advertises it so the dangerous window is zero rather than minutes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019M5G8xgvZWbLzRPRQk58n5

* 0.7.0 — topic coverage radar on the dashboard

Adds a radar chart showing what the learner's vocabulary is ABOUT, not just how
much of it there is — the comprehensible-input question of "can I read a text
on this topic?".

Data: a hand-authored word -> topic map, 4,806 of 9,032 HSK 1-9 words across 20
topics. Every assignment was made by hand and agrees 178/178 with an
independently written 350-word gold sample; the other 4,226 words were reviewed
and deliberately carry no topic (idioms, generic verbs, function words). The
join was validated empirically against CC-CEDICT: 4,806/4,806 keys resolve to
the simplified headword the plugin stores, and 2,885/2,886 traditional surfaces
resolve back correctly.

Metric is frequency-weighted coverage. A plain word count collapsed every topic
into 4-28% once the HSK 7-9 band tripled the denominator; weighting restores a
usable spread (HSK2 6-20%, HSK4 23-43%, HSK6 60-81%). A second "relative to my
level" mode divides out word difficulty, which otherwise predetermines the
ranking for every learner. Ignored words leave both sides of the ratio.

Three implementation notes, each guarding a real failure:
- chip clicks repaint only the section; render() empties the view root, which
  would throw the user back to the top of the dashboard on every click
- saving is leading+trailing debounced: saveSettings() rewrites the whole
  data.json, and the leading edge keeps a single toggle durable even where
  onClose() never fires (iOS deferred views)
- topicRadarTopics is a flat top-level array because settings merge with a
  shallow spread, so a nested object gaining a key later returns undefined

Licence chain is MIT throughout; topic assignments are original work. Coverage
rises: functions 84.33 -> 86.14, branches 80.76 -> 83.36.

entry.title: 0.6.1 — stop rewriting the whole data blob to count launches (#69)
entry.content:
0.6.1 — stop rewriting the whole data blob to count launches (#69)

Crash protection stored its counter in the main data blob, so every healthy
launch did this before Obsidian could show the ribbon icon:

  parse 4.76 MB   crash probe reads data.json
  write 3.2 MB    counter 0 -> 1
  parse 4.76 MB   onloadInner re-reads the same file
  ... 30 s later ...
  parse 4.76 MB   reset reads it again
  write 3.2 MB    counter 1 -> 0

Three full parses and two multi-megabyte writes to store one integer that is
0 before and 0 after. On a synced vault it also re-uploaded a 4.9 MB file on
every launch of every device.

Crash state now lives in its own ~30-byte file next to the plugin. The probe
no longer touches data.json at all, so onloadInner's read is the only parse
on the critical path — and there is no reordering hazard, because nothing
writes between them.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE

The write stays AWAITED. The increment has to be durable before any risky
work runs or the guard cannot see the crash it exists to catch, which is why
localStorage was rejected: setItem returns before its backing store flushes,
and a crash in that window loses the increment — exactly the case this
protects against. Threshold, reset delay, notices and fail-open behaviour are
all untouched; only the storage location and its size moved.

decideOnLoad() is pure, so every branch of a mechanism that can disable the
plugin is directly testable. 16 tests cover both threshold boundaries (4 -> 5
proceeds, 5 -> 6 trips, matching the previous behaviour exactly), a six-crash
simulation that must still auto-disable, fifty healthy launches that must not,
the durability ordering localStorage would have broken, and fail-open on a
missing, corrupt, junk-valued or throwing file.

manifest.dir is optional in Obsidian's API, so the path falls back to
vault.configDir rather than resolving to "undefined/crash-state.json".

Legacy __crashCounter / __autoDisabled keys are dropped from the blob once,
off the critical path, so a downgrade cannot re-read a stale auto-disable
flag. The old count is deliberately not carried over: a user in a live crash
loop is already auto-disabled rather than launching a new version.

Not claimed: that this is the ~4 s iOS startup. On macOS it is ~24 ms of CPU;
the Files-provider I/O cost on iOS is not measurable from here. It removes
6.4 MB of writes per launch either way.

entry.title: 0.6.0 — tell a new user why their Progress chart is empty (#66)
entry.content:
0.6.0 — tell a new user why their Progress chart is empty (#66)

A first vault index inventories every Chinese word already in the notes and
marks them as a baseline, so a brand-new user sees cards reporting thousands
of words above a chart that is a flat line at zero. That reads as breakage.
It is not — the chart plots classifying, and they have not classified
anything yet.

progressEmptyHint() says so when every selected series totals zero, naming
the indexed count so it also replaces the "Tracked excludes N words" note
rather than stacking a second line beneath it. Once anything is classified
the hint disappears and the old note returns.

Deliberately kept to the smallest safe shape, since this ships without
manual testing: the decision is a pure function with no dependencies and no
way to throw, unit-tested across all four states (fresh index, nothing
indexed, has history, no series selected), and the rendering is a single
createEl identical to the two beside it. The one existing line touched is
the summary, which now reads its per-series totals from the same array the
hint does instead of recomputing them — same values, one source.

entry.title: 0.6.0 — make the Cumulative chart cumulative to date, not to the wind…
entry.content:
0.6.0 — make the Cumulative chart cumulative to date, not to the window (#65)

bucketTimestamps() drops every stamp older than its first bucket, and
renderProgressArea() then accumulated from zero at the window's left edge.
So "Cumulative" meant "cumulative within whatever window is selected": the
12-month view only looked right because this learner's classifying happened
to fall inside it, while the 30-day view plotted a flat line on the floor
and a summary reading "Last 30 days: Known 0" under it. A running total of
vocabulary should never fall when you zoom in.

Pre-existing since 0.1.20 (git log -S "acc += d.count"), not a regression
from the Traditional work.

Fixed by supplying the opening balance. countBeforeWindow() counts the
stamps the window discards, and the accumulator is seeded with it.

Two deliberate choices, both about not breaking what already works:

- No existing signature or return shape changes. countBeforeWindow() is a
  new export, `prior` is optional on the series objects, and the bars
  renderer is untouched — its per-period counts are correct as they are.
- The cutoff is an INSTANT, not a comparison against the first bucket's
  key. Week keys are `yyyy-Www`, which do not sort across a year boundary
  ("2026-W01" < "2025-W52"), so a string comparison would have silently
  miscounted every January.

Tests came first: bucketTimestamps had no direct coverage, so its current
behaviour is pinned before anything moved. The boundary between the balance
and the window is then asserted as a property rather than from hand-computed
dates — a binary search finds the first in-window instant and checks that
countBeforeWindow() excludes exactly it and claims the millisecond before,
across day/week/month, two year boundaries and a leap day. The accumulator
is extracted as cumulativeCounts() so it can be tested at all; these tests
run without a DOM.

Also makes an active note scope visible. It filters every number on the
dashboard, but the only sign of it was the dropdown up in the header —
scroll past that and a scoped dashboard is indistinguishable from one that
has lost your vocabulary, which is exactly how it read. There is now a line
above the cards naming the note, with a button back to all vocabulary.

0.6.0 — fix the rc.5 script rows, gate the re-index offer, refresh lint tooling (#64)

* 0.6.0 — refresh the lint toolchain before the stable release

typescript-eslint 8.61.1 -> 8.70.0 and eslint 9.39.4 -> 9.39.5.

typescript-eslint is the one that matters: its minors add and widen rules,
so Obsidian's cloud auto-review can run checks we do not — exactly the
failure mode eslint.config.mjs exists to prevent. 8.70.0 is inside
eslint-plugin-obsidianmd's ^8.35.1 peer range, and the bump surfaces
nothing: still 0 errors, 0 warnings.

eslint-plugin-obsidianmd is already on 0.4.2, which is current. eslint 10
exists but the plugin's peer is >=9.19.0, so it is not required, and a
major flat-config bump immediately before a stable release is risk with no
upside — took the 9.39.5 patch instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019M5G8xgvZWbLzRPRQk58n5

* 0.6.0 — fix the script rows behaving like checkboxes instead of radios

The overflow menu stays open after a toggle and is never rebuilt, so the
three script rows added in rc.5 never repainted each other. Picking
Traditional while Automatic was checked left BOTH ticked, and clicking the
already-active row unticked its own box while the early-return kept the
setting unchanged — leaving the active script showing as off until the menu
was reopened. Visible on the first tap of a feature this release is built
around.

checkRow now returns its checkbox so a caller can repaint a
mutually-exclusive group, and the script rows re-assert all three from the
setting after every click, including the no-op one.

Also stops offering a pointless re-index. Automatic and Traditional build
the identical trie, so moving between them changes what is displayed but
not what is indexed, and the offer would walk the whole vault to report "0
new exposures". indexedSetChanged() lives next to planScriptChange() in the
pure module so it is testable, and gates all three paths: the settings tab
(which needed the previous value threaded through persist, since the new
one is already written by then), the reading view, and the settings-mirror
notice — the last still tells the user their script changed, it just drops
the button when there is nothing to re-index.

And makes trackedBaselineRepaired device-local. It is bookkeeping about
work this device has done, exactly like vaultIndexed beside it in
FILTER_OUT; sharing it would let one device's completed baseline pass
suppress another's, which has its own records to adopt.

entry.title: 0.6.0 — Automatic script mode as the default, and a Progress chart th…
entry.content:
0.6.0 — Automatic script mode as the default, and a Progress chart that stops lying (#63)

Two changes that interleave across the same files.

## Automatic script

Every script problem this release has chased — Traditional notes
shattering into single characters, the junk records that produced, the
skip added to avoid them, re-indexing after a flip, the "this note looks
Traditional" prompt — exists only because the trie was gated on a global
setting. Automatic removes the gate: index both scripts, never convert
anything for display, show each word the way it was read.

Measured against the full CC-CEDICT before committing to it, because it
becomes the default. Indexing both scripts leaves Simplified segmentation
byte-identical: 0 differing tokens across a 22,569-token corpus. Only 392
of 76,783 union-only surfaces can occur in Simplified text at all — the
rest contain a character that is never a simplified headword — and those
392 only ever MERGE what the simplified-only trie split (乾杯 as one token
rather than 乾 + 杯), which is a better answer, not a different one. Cost:
121,275 -> 198,058 keys, 34 -> 65 ms build, +29.3 MB heap.

That cost lands on every upgrading user, not just new installs: 0.6.0
never shipped stable, so nobody has a stored scriptVariant for the
defaults spread to preserve. Deliberate, and called out in the docs.

tsc enumerated the AI work rather than us guessing it: scriptVariant fed
four two-value sites, all of which stopped compiling. resolveAiScript()
decides from the target words, since generation must commit to one script
and has no note to look at.

## Vault-index records are a baseline, not events

Indexing a 2,833-file vault created 9,829 records at once, all stamped
firstSeenAt = now, so the Progress chart's Tracked line showed a vertical
cliff claiming the learner met 9,829 words in a day.

Back-dating from file mtime was tried and rejected on measurement: that
vault's timestamps span 5 months with 47% in one, and its oldest file is
NEWER than the vocabulary history it would have to explain — Nextcloud
rewrote them. It would have turned one honest cliff into two plausible
fictions.

So records a bulk scan created are marked `backfilledAt` and excluded from
Tracked, with the count reported under the chart. A one-shot pass, gated
on `trackedBaselineRepaired`, adopts records an earlier build's index left
behind; one-shot because leaving it on would keep swallowing genuinely
newly-read words on every later index.

## Four things that would have shipped as bugs

- The overflow menu wrote "traditional"/"simplified" from one checkbox. In
  Automatic it renders unchecked, so two taps silently dropped the reader
  into the one mode where a Traditional note shatters. Three explicit rows
  now, which also makes the third state reachable.
- StoryGenerator wrote `script: ${script}` into note frontmatter and would
  have recorded a literal "auto" over Traditional prose.
- displaySurface's `if (script !== "traditional")` would have routed
  Automatic silently down the Simplified path.
- mergeForSync and mergeRecords both build explicit object literals, so
  `backfilledAt` missing from either would have been dropped on every sync
  — working locally and evaporating between devices. Asserted directly.

entry.title: 0.6.0 — test the dictionary and tokenizer against real CC-CEDICT data…
entry.content:
0.6.0 — test the dictionary and tokenizer against real CC-CEDICT data (#62)

Every test in this repo drove a hand-written stub: a three-entry
dictionary, a tokenizer that called every character a word. That leaves a
whole class of bug invisible, because the stub agrees with the code and
neither agrees with CC-CEDICT. The 0.6.0 flashcard bug is the case in
point — VocabularyStore.ensure() seeds lookup()[0].traditional into
rec.surfaces, CC-CEDICT orders entries by codepoint, so 干 seeded the
obsolete 乹 and displaySurface() showed it. It was found by reading code,
not by a failing test, and its regression test still simulates the seeding
with a literal.

Adds a committed ~200-entry CC-CEDICT subset and wires the real pieces
together over it: parseCedict → DictionaryService → Trie →
LatticeTokenizer → scriptDetect / displayForms. 16 tests covering entry
ordering, the real variant counts, the u:/-iu pinyin repair, the Taiwan
reading lifted out of its gloss, segmentation of a Traditional note in
both script modes, script detection including the documented
below-threshold miss, and displaySurface over records built exactly the
way ensure() builds them.

Three of those failed on first run. Two were fixture artifacts —
isTraditionalMarker() is "in byTraditional and not in bySimplified", so a
character whose own entry was missing from the subset reported a marker
status it does not really have (乾 and 裡 are simplified headwords in
their own right). Fixed by pulling in every character of the test notes.
The third was mine: I asserted lookup("绿")[0].pinyin is lǜ, but 绿 is
polyphonic and CC-CEDICT's order between lu:4 and lu4 is not ours to
assume — the same mistake displaySurface() used to make with traditional
variants. Now asserted as membership, with a global check that no entry
anywhere still carries a raw u: or stray tone digit.

Licensing: NOTICE.md says the plugin does not bundle CC-CEDICT, and that
stays true. The generator keeps the simplified/traditional/pinyin mapping
and replaces every English gloss with a placeholder — the same line
build-hsk-map.mjs takes, importing the HSK term→level mapping and nothing
else. The one verbatim field is the "Taiwan pr. [...]" reading, because
that formatted field is itself what extractTaiwanReading() parses. The
fixture is read by tests only and does not reach main.js.

Also documents, as an assertion rather than a comment, why the indexer
skips a whole note rather than filtering tokens: under Simplified a
Traditional note shatters into shards like 公 / 乾 / 程 / 喜, which are
ordinary simplified headwords, so no per-token predicate can tell them
from real vocabulary.

entry.title: 0.6.0 — skip wrong-script notes when indexing, announce a synced scri…
entry.content:
0.6.0 — skip wrong-script notes when indexing, announce a synced script change (#61)

* 0.6.0 — skip notes written in the other script instead of indexing them wrong

DictionaryService.lookup() consults both the simplified and traditional
maps regardless of the setting, but only the trie is gated on
scriptVariant. So with Simplified selected a Traditional note found no
multi-character trie match, fell through to the single-character OOV edge,
and every one of those characters still resolved through lookup() — so
isWord was true and the indexer recorded it. 學, 習, 灣 each became a
permanent vocabulary record, and since indexing only ever adds, nothing
removed them again.

Skip those notes instead, reusing looksTraditional() — already the
conservative one-directional detector the "this note looks Traditional"
prompt uses. The check runs before tokenizing, so a skipped file costs a
character scan rather than a full segmentation pass, which is also why
indexVault now calls dictionary.ensureLoaded() up front: the first
tokenize() used to be what forced the load.

One-directional on purpose — Traditional mode indexes a union of both
scripts, so Simplified notes are never skipped.

Progress carries a `skipped` count and the notice names the fix:
"skipped 3 that look Traditional. Switch Text script to index them."

Not covered, and documented as such: the detector needs three distinct
traditional-only characters, so a very short note still slips through;
this guards the bulk path only, not live reading; and entries created by
an earlier index stay.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019M5G8xgvZWbLzRPRQk58n5

* 0.6.0 — say so when another device changes the script

scriptVariant is a shared setting, so flipping it on one device flips them
all. The remote path was already correct — SettingsMirror.applyMerge()
routes through saveSettingsSilently() into applyScriptSideEffects(), so
the trie really is rebuilt — but it was completely silent: the second
device's reader re-segmented and its flashcards switched script with no
explanation.

planScriptChange() gains a `remote` input and a `notifyRemote` output, so
the decision stays in the pure module that already exists to make this
testable. main threads `remote` through saveSettingsSilently(); the
settings mirror is the only caller that sets it.

The notice reuses offerReindexAfterScriptChange(), now taking a reason, so
it is one notice rather than two. Offering the re-index on the remote path
is safe as of the previous commit's idempotent index — the original
objection was a surprise bulk write on an idle device, and that is gone.
It is still only a button.

Also stops sharing traditionalPromptDismissed. It is a per-device UI
dismissal, so syncing it meant "Don't ask again" on one device silenced
the prompt on every other one. scriptVariant and pronunciationRegion keep
syncing — those describe the vault, which is the same everywhere.

entry.title: 0.6.0 — idempotent vault re-index, and act on the Traditional script …
entry.content:
0.6.0 — idempotent vault re-index, and act on the Traditional script check (#60)

* 0.6.0 — make re-indexing the vault safe to re-run

The script setting offers to re-index, and re-indexing called
recordExposure() once per occurrence. That increments unconditionally, so
a second pass doubled seenCount for every word in the vault, back-dated
lastSeenAt to "now", and spiked today's dailySeenCounts for reading that
never happened. None of it undoable. It also made trying Traditional mode
on a real vault a one-way door.

Add VocabularyStore.recordNoteScan(), which takes a note's whole tally and
reconciles it against the count already stored for that path. A note's
count is a high-water mark: delta <= 0 writes nothing at all — no
timestamp, no updatedAt, no save — so re-running over unchanged text is a
true no-op. A note that grew contributes only the difference; a note that
shrank keeps its count, because unwinding would mean removing exposures
from dailySeenCounts and nothing records which day they were read on.

That last point is also why seenCount is kept in step with
dailySeenCounts rather than derived some other way: mergeForSync()
re-derives seenCount as the sum of the daily counts on every merge, so
any scheme that let the two drift would have its totals silently reset on
the next sync.

recordExposure() is unchanged — live reading has no note total to
reconcile against and must keep incrementing. VaultIndexer now tallies per
file, and progress.recorded becomes the number of NEW exposures, so the
notice reads "0 new exposures" on a clean re-index.

Counts already inflated by an earlier re-index stay inflated; the
high-water mark cannot tell an inflated count from a real one after the
fact. Documented in docs/traditional-chinese.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019M5G8xgvZWbLzRPRQk58n5

* 0.6.0 — act on the Traditional script check instead of discarding it

StoryValidator computed `wrongScript` and its comment claimed the finding
"lets the repair loop try again". It did not. The flag was absent from
both `score` and `ok`, it only appended to `report.notes`, and nothing
anywhere reads `notes` — not StatsView, not StoryGenerator. The repair
loop keyed on missing target words alone. So a model that ignored the
Traditional instruction was detected and the detection thrown away.

Put `wrongScript` on ValidationReport, fail `ok` on it, dock the score so
best-of-N prefers a correct-script candidate on a tie, and let the repair
loop run for it. The trigger is zero traditional-only characters across
the whole story, which a text of these lengths never hits by accident, and
maxRepairIterations caps the retries either way.

The repair prompt needed the same honesty: a story can come back for the
script alone with every target word present, and opening with "your
attempts repeatedly miss required target words" would aim the model at a
problem it does not have. It now leads with the actual defect and names it.

Also makes the mnemonic modal script-aware. It keyed on surfaces[0], so a
Traditional reader got a heading and an AI prompt about the Simplified
form. Display and the prompt now follow displaySurface(); storage stays on
surfaces[0], because updateMnemonic() goes through ensure() and handing it
a converted form would push that form into rec.surfaces — and
surfaces[0]-as-first-encounter is exactly the signal displaySurface()
relies on to avoid showing a guessed variant.

* 0.6.0 — fix pinyin tone placement, stranded ü digits, and Trie surrogate handling
Three pre-existing correctness bugs found while verifying the Traditional Chinese work. All predate this release and affect every user.
1. -iu tone marks landed on the wrong vowel. numbersToToneMarks ranked vowels a > o > e > i > u, but the rule for -iu/-ui is to mark the LAST vowel. Core HSK 1-3 vocabulary was wrong in the shipped data: 六 lìu, 九 jǐu, 牛奶 níu nǎi, 休息 xīu xi, 秋天 qīu tiān, 丢 dīu.
2. Every ü syllable kept a raw tone digit. The downloader converted CC-CEDICT's "u:" to ü AFTER numbersToToneMarks, whose character class has no ":", so "nu:3" never matched and became the literal "nü3". 1,069 entries: 女 nü3, 绿 lü4, 律 lü4.
3. Trie.insert walked code points while Trie.matchesFrom walks code units, so any word containing a character outside the BMP was stored under a key the matcher could never reach. 268 simplified headwords and 10 traditional-only forms never matched.
4,788 of 125,052 entries display wrong pinyin. repairPinyin() fixes them at index time, so existing users get correct pinyin on next load with no dictionary re-download; the downloader fix covers fresh downloads.
The repair is vocabulary-key-safe, which is the constraint that dictates the implementation. toneMarksToNumbers now absorbs a trailing digit as its syllable's tone, so "nü3" and "nǚ" hash identically. Verified against all 125,052 shipped entries: 4,788 repaired, 0 vocabulary keys moved, 0 case or letter damage. Without that change the same repair would have moved 1,066 keys and orphaned those records. The repair is also deliberately NOT a round-trip through numbersToToneMarks, which lowercases and would corrupt 23,485 proper nouns (Qū -> qū, 3D -> 3d).
Dictionary overrides are keyed by makeKey and, unlike WordRecords, are never re-derived on load, so they get a one-shot re-key. It is a pure string transform because onload() runs vocab.load() long before the dictionary is read — forcing an early load would add a ~17 MB read to every startup. Verified: 1,066 of 1,066 legacy keys map correctly, 0 false positives.
Also lands the groundwork for Taiwan readings: DictionaryEntry.pinyinTaiwan, extracted at index time from the "Taiwan pr. [le4 se4]" gloss CC-CEDICT already ships. 512 of 513 entries parse cleanly; the one skip is a prose note with no bracketed reading. Costs 6 ms (repair) + 5 ms (extraction) at load, against 41 ms just to JSON.parse the file.
346 tests pass; lint 0 errors, 0 warnings.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QcoqjUfHtUJ7VAuSyAF99A
* 0.6.0 — script/region settings, Traditional tokenization, and display helpers
Makes the plugin able to read Traditional Chinese (#57). Defaults are unchanged, so an upgrading Simplified user gets a bit-identical trie.
Settings: `scriptVariant` and `pronunciationRegion` as a top-level "Script & region" group placed right after Display — a Traditional reader has to find this before anything else works for them, so it must not sit behind an Advanced sub-page. Both are top-level scalars, so the shallow DEFAULT_SETTINGS spread in onload fills them for existing users with no migration and no schemaVersion bump.
Tokenizer: DictionaryService.surfaces() gains an opt-in `includeTraditional`, and it is a UNION rather than a swap — Traditional readers still meet Simplified text, and mixed vaults have to keep working without a per-note switch. Verified against the real 125k-entry dictionary: 台灣的天氣很熱 was 台|灣|的|天|氣|很|熱 and is now 台灣|的|天氣|很|熱; 圖書館, 學習, 網路 and 軟體 all merge correctly, and every simplified sample segments byte-identically.
lookup() now concatenates the traditional map after the simplified one instead of `simplified ?? traditional`, recovering the sense that was silently dropped for the 66 surfaces that are both a simplified headword and someone else's traditional form (著, 乾, 宁, 於 …). The ordering is fixed and must never depend on a setting: VocabularyStore.ensure() keys records off lookup()[0], so a settings-dependent order would re-key those records on every toggle. Measured across all 66: candidates[0] is unchanged.
Invalidation is centralised in applyScriptSideEffects(), called from saveSettingsSilently(). Four paths can change the script — the settings tab, the view toolbar, importSettings(), and a remote SettingsMirror apply — and the last two replace settings wholesale and then only refresh views, so a script flip arriving that way would repaint fresh colors over a stale trie with no error anywhere. One guard off one remembered value covers all four. VocabularyStore.clearSurfaceCache() is now public for the same reason: DictionaryService.reload() has eight call sites and none could reach it.
displayForms.ts deliberately never converts between scripts. 1,078 simplified headwords map to more than one traditional form, CC-CEDICT orders entries by codepoint rather than frequency, and frequencyRank is never populated — so taking the first candidate gives 发 -> 發 (wrong for 头发), 干 -> 乹 and 历 -> 厤 (obsolete variants), 里 -> 裏 (the Hong Kong form). It returns a form the learner actually encountered instead, and offers the counterpart only when the mapping is unambiguous.
scriptDetect.ts is one-directional by design. The symmetric test does not work: 台, 只, 后 and 里 are simplified headwords yet normal in Taiwan writing, so a "looks simplified" score misfires — a pure Traditional paragraph scored 7 against 4, and 你好我是人今天 read as simplified.
387 tests pass; lint 0 errors, 0 warnings.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QcoqjUfHtUJ7VAuSyAF99A
* 0.6.0 — Traditional parity in the reader, flashcards, stats, and AI
Closes the places where a Traditional reader would have got a worse experience than a Simplified one.
Reader: the word popup's headword is now the form the learner actually tapped, and the counterpart script is shown as a meta row only when the mapping is unambiguous. RubyWidget resolves pinyin through displayPinyin, so the Taiwan reading reaches the page and a region flip correctly busts widget equality.
Flashcards were the worst gap — StatsView drew rec.simplified, so a Taiwan learner was drilled on Simplified characters. They now show the encountered form, and read pinyin through the live dictionary rather than the record's snapshot, which predates both the tone repair and the Taiwan field.
Stats: the search box matched r.simplified only, so typing 學習 found nothing; it now matches every surface. The note-scope filter compared r.simplified against noteSurfaces, which holds raw token surfaces and is therefore traditional in a traditional note — scoped stats came back empty. It now matches on any surface. StatsView also gains invalidateCaches(), because refreshStatsViews() only re-renders and would otherwise keep serving note-scope surfaces and example sentences computed under the old trie.
(loadTriageContext needed no change after all — it already tries every entry of rec.surfaces, so example sentences were being found in traditional notes.)
AI: buildUserPrompt and buildRepairPrompt take the script, and the repair prompt no longer hardcodes "the exact simplified-Chinese surface form". The clause asks for Taiwanese Mandarin usage rather than only Traditional glyphs — characters alone yield Mainland vocabulary in Traditional clothing, and CC-CEDICT carries both halves of every common pair (網路/網絡, 影片/視頻).
validateStory accepts a target in either script, so a model that ignores the instruction is still scored on whether it used the word, and the generated note's checklist ticks on either form so the boxes are truthful. The script check tests for the PRESENCE of traditional-only characters rather than the absence of simplified ones: 台, 只, 后 and 里 are simplified headwords yet entirely normal in Traditional writing, so the absence test is unreliable. Advisory only — a short story can legitimately contain none.
Discoverability, three ways: the settings group, a one-tap "Traditional characters" toggle in the reading view's overflow menu (which runs the full invalidation rather than the plain redecorate the colour checkboxes use), and a conservative one-time prompt when an opened note contains at least three traditional-only characters. The prompt never switches on its own.

* 0.6.0 — docs and version bump for the first release candidate
Adds docs/traditional-chinese.md, linked from the new settings group via docLink() and from the README's guide list, plus a short README section.
The doc is explicit about the two things a Taiwan learner would otherwise discover the hard way: the Taiwan readings cover CC-CEDICT's ~500 idiosyncratic re-readings and NOT the neutral-tone difference you actually hear most (謝謝 xièxiè, 東西 dōngxī), and HSK is a Mainland standard so the colours, "Top HSK" label and story level are calibrated to a syllabus they do not use.
It also explains why the plugin never converts between scripts, with the data behind it: 1,078 Simplified headwords map to more than one Traditional form, and with no frequency data the naive conversion gives 干 -> 乹 and 历 -> 厤.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QcoqjUfHtUJ7VAuSyAF99A
* 0.6.0 — fix regressions found in self-review of the Traditional work
Four defects found reviewing the 0.6.0 branch against 0.5.1, three of them introduced by this branch.
1. WordPopup could freeze after marking a word. refresh() read the surface back out of the rendered headword and called vocab.bySurface() with it. That was safe while the headword was always rec.simplified, but this branch let displaySurface return the counterpart form for an unambiguous mapping — a form the learner may never have encountered, and therefore absent from rec.surfaces, which is what bySurface() falls back to scanning. The popup now remembers the tapped surface and both renders and re-reads by it, so the headword is exactly the characters on the page and refresh() no longer depends on the DOM. Guarded by a test asserting that displaySurface can legitimately return a form outside rec.surfaces.
2. index() could throw on a hand-edited dictionary file. It now reads e.definitions to extract the Taiwan reading, but the vault-side loader only validates `simplified` and `pinyin`. A truncated or hand-written .cci-dictionary.json entry would have thrown mid-load and taken the plugin's dictionary with it. extractTaiwanReading is now defensive about a missing or non-string definitions list.
3. pronunciationRegion had the same silent-path bug the script guard was built to fix. It was handled only in the settings tab, so a region change arriving via importSettings() or a remote SettingsMirror apply left the RubyWidget's snapshotted pinyin stale. Both settings now run through one applyScriptSideEffects() guard, which rebuilds the trie only when the script actually changed and drops cached tokens for either.
4. The Words table still printed the raw r.pinyin snapshot, so it showed pre-repair readings (nü3) and ignored the Taiwan region while the flashcard, popup and detail modal all used the corrected path. It now goes through displayPinyin like everything else. The table is capped at 500 rows, so the extra lookups are bounded.
Also moved StatsView.invalidateCaches() out of the middle of the field declarations.
Regression evidence against the real 125,052-entry dictionary: - lookup()[0] identical for all 198,106 surfaces, so no makeKey can move. - 0 entries whose canonical key changes after the pinyin repair. - 0 segmentation differences over 20,000 synthetic sentences in Simplified mode, and 0 over the 109 CJK spans of the real vault note. - New upgradeRegression.test.ts covers the 0.5.1 -> 0.6.0 path: a record keyed 女|nü53 re-keys to 女|nü3, an old-key and new-key pair for the same word merge into one (strongest status wins, exposure counts summed) rather than duplicating, untouched records are preserved byte for byte, and a traditional surface still resolves to the same record.

* 0.6.0 — make the invalidation guard testable, and verify the wiring end to end
The script/region invalidation decision was the subtlest thing on this branch and the only piece with no test, because it lived inside a method on CciPlugin that a unit test cannot stand up. Extracted to a pure planScriptChange() in settings/scriptChange.ts and covered, including the property that matters: whenever either setting actually moved, retokenize is never false. Getting that wrong repaints fresh colours over stale segmentation and reports nothing.
The extraction also records the asymmetry explicitly — a script change rebuilds the trie because segmentation changes, a region change does not, but BOTH must drop cached tokens because RubyWidget snapshots its pinyin at construction time.
Verified end to end against the real 125,052-entry dictionary, driving the actual DictionaryService + TokenizerService rather than the pieces: - Simplified mode, traditional text: 台|灣|的|天|氣|很|熱|我|昨天|去|圖|書|館|學|習|中文 - After the flip: 台灣|的|天氣|很|熱|我|昨天|去|圖書館|學習|中文 - Simplified text before vs after the flip: character-for-character identical - Flipping back WITHOUT invalidate() returns the stale traditional segmentation, which is direct evidence the guard is load-bearing rather than defensive; invalidate() restores the correct result - 垃圾 reads lā jī / lè sè by region through the real lookup path - 女 indexes as nǚ and 九 as jiǔ with no dictionary re-download - The detector answers true on the traditional sample and false on the simplified one - Whole run, including reading and parsing the 17 MB dictionary: 326 ms
Also confirmed main.js is gitignored, so the release workflow's clean build is what ships rather than a stale local artifact.
410 tests pass; lint 0 errors, 0 warnings; check-release 40 passed, 0 failed.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QcoqjUfHtUJ7VAuSyAF99A
* 0.6.0 — don't let the override migration touch the mirror before bootstrap
Three sync-path defects found while deciding whether this was ready to prerelease. The first is the serious one.
1. The onload override migration wrote through saveDictionaryUserData(), which flushes via vocab.flushSave() and therefore SCHEDULES A MIRROR WRITE. At that point bootstrapMirrorAfterLoad() has not run, so the vault mirror still holds a remote envelope this device has never merged — writing local-only vocabulary over it loses whatever another device had. The 5s mirror debounce means bootstrap usually wins the race, but "usually" is not a guarantee on a mobile device with stalled Nextcloud I/O, which is exactly the environment this plugin documents elsewhere as hostile. It now writes the plugin data blob directly and leaves the mirror alone; the corrected keys reach it on the next natural write, after the merge.
The same call was also a floating promise. An unhandled rejection during onload surfaces as Obsidian's generic "plugin encountered an error while loading" — the failure mode vocab.load() already carries a comment about. Errors are now caught and logged; the migration is idempotent, so a failed write just means it runs again next launch.
2. Remote overrides bypassed the migration entirely. The onload pass only sees this device's own blob, but mergeMirroredDictionaryData() inserts whatever the mirror holds verbatim — so a peer still on 0.5.1 would re-introduce legacy keys after every sync, silently re-orphaning those overrides. Incoming overrides are now migrated on the way in.
3. Wired clearSurfaceCache() into all eight dictionary.reload() sites. This is the pre-existing bug noted during review: reload() changes what lookup() resolves a surface to, bySurface() memoises that, and nothing ever cleared it — so a newly added custom word could keep resolving to a cached miss until some unrelated vocabulary mutation happened to flush it.

* 0.6.0 — never show a dictionary-guessed traditional form
displaySurface() treated every entry of record.surfaces as a form the learner had actually read, and returned it before reaching the distinctTraditionalForms() === 1 ambiguity guard.
surfaces is not that. VocabularyStore.ensure() seeds lookup(surface)[0] .traditional into it at record creation, and CC-CEDICT orders entries by codepoint rather than frequency, so entries[0].traditional is an obsolete or wrong-sense variant for 539 headwords — 346 of them single characters. Reading 干 in a Simplified note therefore produced surfaces ["干","乹"], and Traditional mode drilled the learner on 乹 across flashcards, the words table, story targets and the frontmatter checklist. Same for 历 -> 厤, 里 -> 裏 (Hong Kong, not Taiwan) and 钟 -> 鍾 (the surname).
Only surfaces[0] is evidence of an encounter — it is the form the word was first met in and is never seeded. Use it, and route everything else through the existing guard.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019M5G8xgvZWbLzRPRQk58n5
* 0.6.0 — keep the Words tab scoped across a script switch
invalidateCaches() emptied noteSurfaces but never re-derived it, while noteScope survived. scopedRecords() only filters while noteSurfaces is non-empty, so a script change silently widened a note-scoped Words tab to the entire vocabulary with the scope selector still naming the note.
Re-run setScope() when a scope is active, and move the call site in applyScriptSideEffects() below clearTokenCache() — re-deriving the scope re-tokenizes that note, which ahead of the clear would just read back the stale cached tokens. Also drops a typeof guard made redundant by the instanceof check next to it.
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com> Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019M5G8xgvZWbLzRPRQk58n5
* 0.6.0 — offer the re-index wherever a person changes the script
Three paths let a user flip scriptVariant — the settings tab, the reading view's overflow menu and the "this note looks Traditional" prompt — but only the first offered to re-index the vault, which is what makes word counts match the new script. Move the offer onto the plugin and call it from all three; deliberately not from applyScriptSideEffects(), so a remote settings-mirror apply stays silent on an idle device. Its button now uses the .cci-notice-actions wrapper the styles were written for.
Also in this file: set lastAppliedScriptVariant / lastAppliedRegion before the accent-derivation save rather than after. saveSettingsSilently() runs applyScriptSideEffects() synchronously, so with a stored "traditional" the old order fired view refreshes during onload, before tokenizer and vocab exist. And drop a duplicated clearSurfaceCache() in mergeMirroredDictionaryData(). Restores persist()'s JSDoc, which the new method had displaced in SettingsTab.

DictionaryOverride.pinyinTaiwan was read by DictionaryService.lookup() but nothing ever wrote it — there was no UI. Add the field to the dictionary editor in override mode, where displayPinyin() will pick it up whenever Pronunciation is set to Taiwan. Custom words have no Taiwan field, so the input is not offered there.
The surface label was derived from the global scriptVariant, but override mode is opened with rec.surfaces[0] — the form the word was FIRST seen in, which can be Simplified while the plugin is set to Traditional. Read it off the entry instead, so the box is not labelled "traditional" over 学习.

entry.content:
0.5.1 — no hanzi in the emoji line, pinyin beside characters in the story (#55)

Two rules added to the fixed mnemonic system prompt, so they also apply to
users who have customised their own user template.

The emoji line must not contain Chinese characters: the word itself is
already displayed right next to the line on the card, so repeating the
hanzi burns the 40-grapheme budget and weakens the cue — which matters
more once the line can be rendered as a third annotation row. The
existing "use a word only where no emoji can carry the idea" clause now
says explicitly that it means an English word.

The story must give tone-marked pinyin in parentheses every time it names
a character. "The child 子 under a roof" is useless to a learner who
cannot read 子 yet; it has to read "the child 子 (zǐ)".

Prompt-only by design. Stripping hanzi in the parser would also mangle a
mnemonic the user typed by hand, and the editor already lets them correct
any model slip.

entry.title: 0.5.1 — clear every Obsidian-checker warning (#54)
entry.content:
0.5.1 — clear every Obsidian-checker warning (#54)

The community-plugin review of 0.5.0 passed releases, dependencies and
build verification but flagged 34 source findings. Our local gate reported
none of them, which was the first thing to fix: we pinned
eslint-plugin-obsidianmd 0.3.0 (35 rules, no prefer-create-el, no
settings-definitions rule) and had switched off
no-unnecessary-type-assertion under a comment claiming the cloud ignored
it. Bumped to 0.4.1 and re-enabled the rule; local lint then reproduced
the cloud's findings exactly, and CI now emits a warning annotation
whenever a newer checker is published so the mirror cannot drift again.

Ten unnecessary type assertions removed. Twenty-three createElement call
sites moved to Obsidian's helpers: a parent's createDiv/createSpan where
one exists at creation time, the global helpers for detached nodes
(CodeMirror widget toDOM, the popup root, toolbar menus). The rule's
autofix was not usable here — it rewrites activeDocument.createElement()
to activeWindow.createSpan(), which does not exist.

The settings tab is now declarative. getSettingDefinitions() describes
every setting, which is what makes them findable from Obsidian's settings
search; display() is deleted because Obsidian skips it entirely for tabs
that return definitions, and minAppVersion moves 1.8.7 → 1.13.0
accordingly. Nested settings are addressed by dotted key through new
getControlValue/setControlValue overrides (settingsPath.ts), with the API
keys routed to the device-local key store via a secret: prefix so they
still never touch data.json. Vault path fields use the built-in
file/folder controls, which retires PathPickers. Blocks with no
declarative equivalent — the formatting picker, status-priority list,
OpenAI usage card, dictionary status — keep their existing imperative
renderers behind render items.

settingsCoverage.test.ts guards the rewrite: it asserts every leaf of
DEFAULT_SETTINGS either has a control or is listed as deliberately
managed elsewhere, that no control binds a path that does not exist, and
that keys are unique. It surfaced that newWordBehavior and
unknownWordBehavior are read nowhere in the plugin; they were absent from
the old tab too, so the dead docs section describing them is removed
rather than a dead control added.

entry.content:
0.5.0 — provider-parity audit fixes before stable (#53)

Pre-stable sweep after 0.5.0-rc.3, which was only tested against OpenAI.

The AI wiring needs no change: every feature funnels through
AiProviderService.chatJson, and MnemonicService calls it exactly like
EnhanceDictionaryService and StoryGenerator do, so provider selection,
endpoint shaping, streaming, timeouts and usage logging are inherited
from paths Ollama already exercises. Three real edge cases came out of
the audit.

MNEMONIC_SCHEMA was invalid under json_schema strict mode. When the user
picks Response format = json_schema, buildResponseFormat sends
strict: true, which rejects an additionalProperties:false object with a
property missing from `required`. `story` was optional, so OpenAI and the
LiteLLM/vLLM proxies people front local models with would reject the
request outright while Ollama's lenient grammar conversion accepted it.
Both properties are now required, matching the shape the system prompt
already declares; the parser still treats a missing story as absent, so
lenient providers are unaffected.

Notices were buried by our own modals. liftModal puts our modal container
at z-index 400, but Obsidian deliberately stacks --layer-notice above
--layer-modal, so any Notice raised while one of our modals was open —
the "Mnemonic failed" error, story-generation failures, the persistent
[CCI AI] debug notice — rendered behind the modal dimmer. The notice
container is lifted to 401 to restore Obsidian's own ordering.

Migrated mnemonics rendered as the literal placeholder "🧠 (story only)",
which after the v3 migration is the state of every pre-0.5.0 prose
mnemonic. The collapsed row now previews the story itself, and the
expand toggle is omitted when it would expand to identical text.

Docs: README tour gains the reader text colors, and the two settings
paths that skipped the "Advanced display" step are corrected.

0 warned; Obsidian-parity lint 0 errors / 0 warnings; 264 tests pass.
Artifacts verified present: main.js, manifest.json, styles.css,
versions.json, LICENSE.

entry.title: 0.5.0 — one Mnemonic button, emoji-first two-field mnemonics (#52)
entry.content:
0.5.0 — one Mnemonic button, emoji-first two-field mnemonics (#52)

Follow-up to 0.5.0-rc.2 testing.

Modal layering, properly this time. rc.2 lifted only MnemonicModal, so
the manual "Mnemonic…" prompt (a bare Modal from confirmInput) still
opened behind the word card. The cause is structural: .cci-popup (100),
.cci-bottom-sheet (200) and .cci-overflow (300) all outrank Obsidian's
--layer-modal, so any modal opened over them is trapped. A liftModal()
helper now tags every modal this plugin opens — confirmAsync, promptAsync,
EditDictionaryModal, GenerateStoryModal, SettingsConflictModal,
MnemonicModal — with the .cci-modal-front container class.

The two mnemonic buttons collapse into one. "Mnemonic" opens an editor
with two fields: a short emoji line (mnemonic.text) and a story
(mnemonic.story). "Generate with AI" fills both in place instead of
locking the result behind a preview, so the user can edit it, reroll, or
discard; nothing persists until Save, and clearing both fields deletes
the mnemonic.

The emoji line is capped at 40 graphemes because a future release may
render it as a third annotation line in place of the English gloss, where
prose would not fit. The system prompt now asks for an emoji sequence
encoding components, tone and meaning, with words only where no emoji can
carry the idea, plus a story that unpacks it. Clamping counts graphemes
via Intl.Segmenter so a cut never lands inside a surrogate pair or a ZWJ
emoji, and never leaves a dangling joiner.

Existing mnemonics are migrated, not destroyed: schema v3 moves a text
too long to be a line into the story field, and only when story is empty
— a record that already has a story keeps both verbatim.
mnemonic.updatedAt is left alone so two-device conflict resolution is
unaffected, and the migration is idempotent and runs on mirror-absorb and
import as well as on load, so a device still on rc.2 cannot undo it.

The card now shows the emoji line whenever one exists, clamped to two
lines, with the story behind a toggle.

entry.title: 0.5.0 — fix mnemonic modal layering and text-color picker visibility …
entry.content:
0.5.0 — fix mnemonic modal layering and text-color picker visibility (#51)

Two defects found testing 0.5.0-rc.1.

Mnemonic modal was trapped behind the word popup, making it impossible to
interact with. Cause: .cci-popup (z-index 100) and, on mobile,
.cci-bottom-sheet (200) sit above Obsidian's --layer-modal, so any modal
opened while the card is up renders underneath. openDictionaryEditor
never hit this because it closes the popup right after .open(); the
mnemonic action omitted that. It now closes the popup the same way, and
MnemonicModal additionally tags its own container with .cci-modal-front
(z-index 400) so it also clears the toolbar overflow menu. The dead
onDone callback goes away with the popup it used to refresh.

The three text-color pickers were rendered only after the enable toggle
was switched on, so an expanded "Advanced display" section showed a lone
toggle and nothing else — the feature read as missing. Pickers and the
reset button now always render; the toggle only decides whether they take
effect. Reset writes straight into the live controls instead of
rerendering the tab, which used to collapse the enclosing details
element.
